A strong defender is vitally important to any successful football team. Sorting out the back-line is crucial, and having some serious defensive talent is a surefire way to build a team destined for silverware. Much focus is placed on attacking players, which is why any list of the best footballers in the world will always be dominated by that type of star.

However, we've highlighted the best defenders in the world right now, in order to give them their flowers for a change. From buccaneering full-backs to commanding centre-halves, the beautiful game is laced with talented defenders in all shapes and sizes. Here are the best players who operate at the back in a role that has been unsung for too long.

Given that trying to separate those on the list is such a difficult task, a number of factors will be taken into consideration as to where they end up in the rankings. These include:

The imposing France international is a great example of the modern centre back: athletic, composed, and complete with impressive attributes that exceed his defensive capabilities. Dayot Upamecano built a formidable duo alongside Ibrahima Konaté at RB Leipzig, leading both to the French national team and transfers to elite European teams.

Upamecano has established himself as a key part of Bayern Munich's defensive setup, securing several league titles and domestic cup triumphs since his move in 2021. With France, Upamecano has featured regularly, winning the Nations League in 2021 and playing the entire 120 minutes of France's World Cup final loss to Argentina in 2022. In 2026, he was one of nine defenders to be nominated for the Ballon d'Or.

Luka Vuskovic has been a revelation since joining Brighton & Hove Albion in the summer of 2026. The Croatian has been tipped for great things since a loan spell at Hamburg put him on the Seagulls' radar in the first place. Tottenham Hotspur still decided to sell up, however, cashing in for as much as £50m.

Known for his aerial ability, recovery pace and modern passing range, the young defender is already among the very best in his position. The future is certainly bright.

Marc Guehi has been a fine defender for a number of years now but has really established himself at the highest level over the past three seasons.

He performed well for England at Euro 2024, as they made it to the final of the tournament, losing to Spain. He then followed that up by captaining Crystal Palace to their first-ever major trophy, as they defeated Liverpool in the FA Cup final, before beating them again to win the Community Shield a few months later.

Guehi earned a big move to Manchester City in 2026 after a 2025 summer move to Liverpool fell through. The England man has since established himself at the heart of the defence, helping the club to win the FA Cup during the 2025/26 season.

Alphonso Davies has been one of the most exciting attacking fullbacks in football for some time now, really breaking into the Bayern Munich team during the 2019/20 season, in which he helped deliver a treble – made up of the Champions League, Bundesliga and the DFB-Pokal.

In total, he has seven league titles under his belt in Germany and has enjoyed a great deal of success with Bayern. The only issue has been fitness problems, as injuries have regularly interrupted his momentum in Munich. Davies will hope to keep himself fit if he wants to move higher up this list.

Riccardo Calafiori has quickly become one of the best defenders in the world. Swapping centre-back for a fullback role at Arsenal, the Italian has often provided a surprise goalscoring threat, combining his instinct inside one area with his defensive prowess in the other. He is among the most undroppable players under Mikel Arteta.

Injuries have threatened to delay his progress, but Calafiori still played a key role as Arsenal finally ended their wait for another Premier League title in the 2025/26 campaign.

While AC Milan are counting their lucky stars that they took a punt on Theo Hernandez’s signature in the summer of 2019, it’s his previous employers, Real Madrid, who will be kicking themselves for letting him go for such a paltry fee. Since moving from Spain to Italy, most fans would agree that Hernandez consistently ranks among the world's best defenders every season.

From Essien to Kaka, here are the 10 greatest players who have played for Real Madrid and AC Milan.

Quick enough to burst forward with ease, while his high IQ allows him to marshal the back line from the left-back berth, the Frenchman has every tool to play at the top level of the sport for the next decade or so. However, a recent move to Al-Hilal may make it difficult for him to keep his place in this list without regularly playing in Europe.

Marc Cucurella has undergone what many would consider to be somewhat of a redemption arc in the last couple of years. At Brighton, he was lauded as one of the best left-backs in the Premier League before his 2022 move to Chelsea led to a decline in form as he came close to being kicked out of Stamford Bridge within a year of his arrival.

What seemed to catapult him back into better form was Spain’s Euro 2024 victory. From that point, the full-back regained his confidence and mojo and, as a result, became an incredibly valuable member of both Chelsea and Spain's squads. After winning the 2026 World Cup with Spain, Cucurella earned a huge move to Real Madrid during the 2026 summer transfer window.

Over the course of the last 24 months, Willian Pacho has transitioned from a young defender looking to show his worth in European football to a winner of the continent’s biggest competition and one of its most highly touted defenders.

The Ecuadorian, who made a name for himself in Belgium and Germany before his big-money move to the French capital in 2024, has settled in at the Stade de France incredibly well. Linking up with the likes of veteran Marquinhos, he has excelled thus far as part of the back-to-back Champions League-winning squad. The future continues to look bright for Pacho.

When Abdukodir Khusanov's header allowed Chelsea to open the scoring just three minutes into his Manchester City debut, many predicted that it would be the defining moment of his Man City career for all the wrong reasons. Since then, however, he has been among the best defenders in the world.

The young centre-back is among the quickest in his position in the Premier League, if not the world, and uses that recovery pace to his advantage. Despite his age and relatively small stature, Khusanov also has no trouble when asked to outmatch opposition forwards on a physical level - winning 60% of his duels in the 2025/26 campaign.

There were some doubts over Ezri Konsa's ability to step up for a side like Arsenal. Those doubts couldn't have been put to bed any quicker if he tried, however.

The England defender has taken a seat at the top table and has not looked back since, having also won the Europa League with Aston Villa in the 2025/26 campaign. At the start of the 2026/27 season, he ensured that the Gunners didn't miss William Saliba during his absence for a single second.

It's worth noting that Konsa is also an England mainstay these days. The centre-back has earned his place for the Three Lions and could be crucial if they are to finally end their wai for silverware.

Ariana Grande’s Flipped Bob Is Fall’s Sweetest Trend

📅 2023-09-25  |  Read Source →

Late last month, Ariana Grande sent shockwaves around the beauty world with a single selfie. The singer, actor, and beauty brand founder had recently gone back to brunette, officially ending her Wicked era. Now, she took it a step further by chopping off her hair.

“After being blonde for so long, her ends were ready to go,” hairstylist Brandon Pietsch tells Vogue of the transformation. Grande’s golden metamorphasis for the role of Glinda in Wicked took place in 2022, and anybody who has dyed their hair for an extended period time knows the toll repeated chemical damage has on hair. So that’s where Pietsch’s shears came in. “This is all her real hair! Ariana’s hair was quite long, I’d say we took a good six inches off. The concept was a soft bob that was short enough to force her to take a break from the pony, paired with a rich, warm color closer to her natural shade. I'm personally obsessed with how the warm shade brings out the dark amber tones in her eyes.”

In the days since, she’s been (mostly) wearing in a singular style: The flipped-out bob. “Retro looks are coming back for fall in full force,” Pietsch says. He describes Grande’s haircut as a soft blunt bob with internal layers that allow her to style in a a variety of ways. With this chop, he also took her a touch closer to her natural shade of brunette. Perhaps her new signature look is brewing?

Grande isn’t the only celebrity going in on the flipped-out bob. Margot Robbie styled her hair in a similar way—with a return of the side bang!—for the Chanel Cruise show that took place in Australia on November 5th. The look, done by her go-to hairstylist Bryce Scarlett, was a sweet take on her somewhat-new blunt bob (and that cut came hot on the heels of the end of her Wuthering Heights tour, are we starting to see a pattern?). French girl extraordinaire Lea Seydoux and Ayo Edebiri have also taken their hair to new degrees with flipped ends.

What makes the look modern and not Stepford Wives is all in the prep and maintenance, according to Pietsch. “Bobs can actually be pretty high maintenance,” he says. Grande and company are wearing their flipped-bobs without a ton of volume at the crown (that was Jackie O’s signature style), but instead close to the head and at a precise angle. “For fall and winter, I'm loving softer, less blunt bobs with internal layering so the hair still has movement. Very ’60s, ’70s and ’90s.”

Although CDs offer less liquidity than a regular checking account or savings account, you might get a higher rate of return with this financial product. This is especially true if you open a CD account with a longer timeline; for example, a 60-month CD instead of a 12-month CD.

According to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), national average CD rates range from 0.23% to 1.81% depending on the CD term, as of writing.

Dry Brushing: Why I Do It Every Day And All The Benefits

📅 2023-09-13  |  Read Source →

It seems like every time I watch a get-ready-with-me video, the first step of the routine is dry brushing. And while I’ve tried it here and there, I never found myself committing to the act. But this skin-care practice is beloved by not only the likes of Gwyneth Paltrow and Tracee Ellis Ross, but also by functional health doctors and medical professionals as well.

So what is dry brushing? It’s the act of running a bristled brush across your skin while working against gravity (so working toward your torso on limbs) to help with moving the body’s lymphatic system.

Everybody raves about the myriad of health benefits that comes along with dry brushing—from physically exfoliating your skin and eliminating strawberry skin to increasing blood flow and potentially diminishing the appearance of circulation.

Perhaps, then, it’s time to really give it a try.

True to its name, dry brushing involves running a bristled brush over dry skin, most commonly on the body (though occasionally, on the face if you’re working with a face-specific brush that’s much softer). “It is a powerful Ayurvedic practice that both exfoliates the skin and opens detox pathways to support lymphatic drainage and boost immunity,” says Lauren Berlingeri, co-founder of HigherDose.

A simple pre-shower ritual, it isn’t just used in Ayurvedic medicine to stimulate the skin and the body’s lymphatic system, but in traditional Chinese medicine (a.k.a. TCM) too. It’s a practice that has stood the test of time, which is always a good sign when trying to understand whether a wellness “trend” is really worth its salt.

As well as stimulating lymphatic drainage, which helps in detoxifying the body, dry brushing is supposed to be effective for removing dead skin cells to smooth skin, boosting blood circulation, and reducing puffiness and water retention. It is a great way to invigorate body and mind, especially at the start of the day. And some say it’s also great at reducing the appearance of cellulite, but from my personal research, this seems somewhat unfounded.

Sophie Bolvary, licensed massage therapist at Sanara, adds that the practice of dry brushing may boost our immune system: “The lymphatic system does not have a ‘pump’ of its own, meaning it only gets working when we start moving our body or when it is stimulated manually by dry brushing or light massage,” she explains.

She adds that different brushes can have a different effect on the body. Dry brushes made with boar-hair bristles are ideal for daily use and exfoliation. Dry brushes with ionic-copper bristles carry the added benefit of sweeping your body in negative ions, which is known for antiviral and antibacterial properties in traditional medicine. It also may bring us full body-mind refreshment as an added self-care benefit.

“The brisk rhythmic motion creates a sensory reset that I find both grounding and energizing,” Bolvary adds. “Helping to sharpen mental alertness and brighten my mood.” Pro tip: Sprinkle an essential-oil blend (like something with citrus) to your dry brush to further wake up your senses.

I’ve used a dry body brush during episodic health kicks previously, but rarely consistently—but my coworker swears by it before every shower, especially when she’s taking an “Everything Shower.” What I’ve most noticed since making it (at least) a four-times-a-week thing is that my skin is infinitely looking more polished and brighter. It’s an excellent way to quickly slough off the dead skin cells that form a grey veil over what was months before a summer tan, and it’s certainly a good way to wake yourself up in the morning.

I have found that combining it with a “contrast” shower—i.e., turning the temperature hot, then cold, then hot, then cold—makes me feel extremely energized, particularly after a vigorous workout. You also don’t really need to commit to doing five minutes to reap the benefits—give it three minutes and you’ll feel fantastic as you start your day. It’s worth noting that—as hard as I willed it—dry brushing won’t stimulate lymphatic drainage enough to cure a hangover. This is deeply disappointing, but I continue to search for a fix.

Newbies to the practice should know that once you’ve dry-brushed, you’ll likely experience an itchy, tingling sensation, along with some possible redness, which soon settles. This feeling quickly becomes less prominent with regular use, but it’s actually a sign that your circulation is revved up and blood is en route to the surface of the skin.

You also might feel, for lack of a better way to phrase it, like your skin is dusty. This is all the dead skin cells you just exfoliated off—which is why most people prefer to do this practice before hopping in the shower. Don’t fret, a little big of your favorite body soap will take care of it.

Dry body brushing is a really easy—and affordable—ritual to commit to, which is why it gets a yes from me. You can’t always see the many benefits it has on the body, but you can often feel them. I have personally noticed a more even skin tone, slightly lighter-feeling legs (not yet as streamlined as Paltrow’s, unfortunately), and more morning vitality. I also firmly believe that taking a few intentional minutes to do something positive for your well-being each day is underrated.

Next up… time to crack body moisturizing. A look at the dry brushes we’d recommend, below.

There are a few negative side effects that can occur if you’re not careful. Marisa Garshick, MD, board-certified dermatologist at MDCS Dermatology, says that it may cause irritation or micro-tears in the skin if too much pressure is applied. You’ll also want to consider what skin conditions you might be dealing with and if your skin type can tolerate all this brushing. Dr. Garshick says it’s not recommended for anyone with sensitive, broken, or inflamed skin like eczema or psoriasis.

Bolvary adds that you’ll want to be mindful about cleaning your brush (more on how to do that later). Because of the exfoliating nature of dry brushing, there could be a lot of skin-shedding debris that builds up in the brush that can make dry brushing ineffective or irritate your skin further.

Dr. Garshick says that dry brushing can be done one to two times a week if you have sensitive skin, as frequent brushing might cause irritation. But if your skin can tolerate it, Bolvary says that it can be a daily practice. She recommends doing it at the start of your day, right before hopping in the shower. “Some people find it more stimulating and energizing than a cup of coffee,” she says. Here’s to hoping.

Dry brushing done by a professional will give you a more in-depth treatment. “The practitioner takes care of the work, and reaches all the hard-to-reach areas, while you simply enjoy the awakening sensations,” says Bolvary. “Also, the practitioner can demonstrate proper technique and pressure for your skin and body type.”

But that doesn’t mean doing it at home won’t have its own benefits. She says it’s helpful to look at a lymphatic glow map: “A very easy Google search, which can outline the general flow of lymph and how to sweep into the main lymph ports of the body.” After a few tries on your own, she says, you get used to it.

Bolvary says that because dry brushes are usually made with natural materials, it’s best to use natural, non-chemical cleaning solutions to clean your brushes. “I like to get a bowl of warm water with several drops of tea tree oil and place the brush bristles down to let it soak for about 30 minutes. Then set it aside to dry.”

But keep in mind that your brush will soften over time and will eventually shed a little with regular washing. “These tools are not meant to last forever,” she says. “So if your brush has become too soft and the bristles are falling out with every use, it may be time for a new one.”

Try to wash your brush once every two weeks and spritz it with something like tea tree mist after every use. Bolvary also recommends leaving it in a window to air-dry rather than on your shower ledge, where it can easily get dirty.

When we test and review a product, we take a holistic approach to deliver well-rounded product recommendations. First, we lean on Vogue’s vast network of experts—from board-certified dermatologists to celebrity estheticians—to gain professional acumen on the industry’s standout products, ones these specialists would actually use on their clients. We pair their expertise with our editorial best practices to curate the thoughtful edits you read on our site.

As it relates to dry brushes, we selected the best based on the following characteristics: bristle type, texture, handle length, size, and the skin and wellness concerns they address. To do this, we paired our own personal tests of each formula with expert guidance and reviewer insights to determine which we would recommend to you. Read more about our testing methodology here.

The 9 Players Ralf Rangnick Recommended to Manchester United

📅 2023-08-21  |  Read Source →

Rob is senior football editor at GiveMeSport, with over 15 years experience covering sport in various capacities since graduating from the University of Gloucestershire in 2008 with a degree in journalism. A childhood obsession for all things football developed into a career writing about the beautiful game, initially producing content for clients including Luton Town Football Club and the PGMOL. His first big interviews were with Premier League referees Howard Webb and Michael Oliver in 2009. He then spent four years producing written content for a betting website, mainly focusing on football, and was there to cover various games and tournaments including the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012. Rob joined GiveMeSport in 2013 (initially as a sub-editor before becoming a senior writer and then senior editor in 2020) and has covered countless football matches and other sporting events, interviewed various high-profile figures including Rio Ferdinand, Peter Crouch and Theo Walcott, and written well over 10,000 articles during that time. Rob has played a key role in GiveMeSport's coverage of the World Cups in 2014, 2018 and 2022, plus Euro 2016, Euro 2020 and Euro 2024, along with many Champions League finals. While football is Rob's area of expertise, he has also covered a wide range of other sports during his time at GiveMeSport including boxing, tennis and darts, as well as the 2016, 2020 and 2024 Olympic Games.

Not many Manchester United supporters will look back at Ralf Rangnick’s time at the helm fondly, though he did all he could to set the club up for a more prominent future. The 68-year-old German, who is currently in charge of the Austrian national team, was appointed the Red Devils’ manager on an interim basis in November 2021 - but ultimately failed to prove his worth.

He was poised to remain at the club in a consultancy role to support Erik ten Hag in his inaugural season in England, but upped and left soon after the Dutchman’s arrival. Rangnick, who has registered the worst points-per-game ratio of all managers to have attempted to steady the ship after Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement (with the exception of Ruben Amorim), took charge of all recruitment-based decisions at RB Leipzig and Red Bull Salzburg but failed to stamp his authority in Manchester in the same regard.

There were, however, a flurry of names that he recommended to the club during his short association, though none of them came to fruition. "Open-heart surgery" is what Rangnick claimed the squad needed during his final weeks at the club, as he made it clear that significant changes were required – and some time down the line, it’s evidently clear that the same issues are still embroiled at Old Trafford.

According to the Daily Mail, there were several names discussed as potential signings by Rangnick, including Manchester City duo Josko Gvardiol and Erling Haaland. But that’s not where the list ends. Some have made alternative high-profile moves, and some are still waiting to be snapped up. Let’s take a look at what they’re all up to now.

Enzo Fernandez is now playing for the blue half of Manchester after joining City from Chelsea for a joint-British record fee of £125 million in the summer.

The 25-year-old played a limited number of games for Benfica before making the move to England in 2023 and showed glimpses of his world-class qualities during his time at Stamford Bridge.

On the international stage, Fernandez was a key part of Lionel Scaloni’s 2022 World Cup-winning squad - even if it was Lionel Messi, one of the greatest football players of all time, who deservedly dominated the headlines during and after the tournament in Qatar. Even prior to that, though, United were reportedly keeping a close eye on the midfielder while he was at River Plate.

However, it's understood that the club were waiting for incoming manager Erik ten Hag to give the green light before signing him. The one (slight) silver lining is that his arrival may have stunted the development of England's Kobbie Mainoo, who has shown that he has the potential to become a top player for club and country - even if things didn't go to plan for him under Ruben Amorim.

United’s local rivals Manchester City are the Premier League club that took a calculated punt on the highly-rated defender. Despite his tender age, Josko Gvardiol starred for Croatia during the 2022 World Cup and rightfully earned praise and, in turn, his big-money move.

The 24-year-old was a domineering asset for his previous club, RB Leipzig, playing 87 games during his stint in Germany. After a shaky start to life in England, he has taken his game to new heights under the stewardship of Pep Guardiola. Given United's continued issues with Luke Shaw, a left-back of this quality going begging is one they may live to regret.

Despite playing second-fiddle to Erling Haaland during his Manchester City stint, Julian Alvarez is now widely regarded as one of the world's best forwards and deservedly so. He caught the eye of various top clubs while playing for River Plate in his native Argentina after notching 85 goal contributions in 122 games and transferred much of that form over to the Etihad Stadium.

Had United acted on Rangnick's advice, though, Alvarez might have been playing for the red side of Manchester instead. Rangnick was reportedly furious when the club failed to secure the Argentine's signature before he signed for City. After 36 goals in 103 appearances for the Sky Blues, he completed an £81 million switch to Atletico Madrid, where he managed to score an impressive 29 goals in his first season with the Spanish club.

Alvarez attempted to force a move to Barcelona in the summer but remains an Atletico player... for now.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Julian Alvarez became the first player in football history to win the Treble and the World Cup in the same season.

Luis Diaz's spell at Liverpool was largely positive, albeit marred ever-so-slightly by inconsistency at times. In his brightest moments, though, the livewire forward was truly electrifying. He haunted the Red Devils on numerous occasions as he has managed five goal contributions in six clashes, with a double coming during the Merseyside club's 3-0 victory at Old Trafford in September 2024. He made the move to Bayern Munich last summer and has hit the ground running in Germany.

Before becoming Jurgen Klopp’s marquee winter signing in 2022, the dynamic Colombian international was one of FC Porto’s driving forces, scoring 41 goals and registering 19 assists for the Portuguese heavyweights - so it’s no wonder that Rangnick had his eye on him. United's loss was undoubtedly Liverpool's gain, as he helped the Reds win a Premier League title.

Of all the missed opportunities, this one will sting the most for the Old Trafford faithful. Erling Haaland has been nothing short of extraordinary for Manchester City following his arrival from Borussia Dortmund. United legend Wayne Rooney even described him as the world's best footballer now that the Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo era has come to an end.

The goal-machine needed just 105 games to score his first 100 Premier League goals, and his links to Old Trafford go even further back than Rangnick's desperate plea. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer confirmed that the domineering forward was a man that the former United boss had told the club to sign long before he took the job in 2018.

As the 2021-22 season came to a close, it was patently clear that reinforcements in midfield were desperately needed at Old Trafford - hence why Konrad Laimer was eyed. At that time, the versatile midfielder had also caught the attention of Bayern Munich, who he eventually signed for, but Manchester United could have saved themselves money and hassle if they elected to sign him back when Rangnick first recommended the Austrian to the club’s higher-ups.

At Bayern, Laimer is a solid rotational option who would likely settle in well at Old Trafford, much like his former teammate Marcel Sabitzer did during his loan spell. Rangnick did at least get the chance to coach the midfielder, as he is a key part of the Austrian national team.

Alvaro Morata, 33, is somewhat of a footballing journeyman, having plied his trade for Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid, Juventus and Chelsea - though he has never quite managed to establish himself as one of Europe’s elite strikers. The Spaniard has scored goals wherever he's played during his career, although profligacy in some of the biggest fixtures has prevented him from establishing a reputation as a truly world-class forward.

The Spaniard was initially linked with a move to the Theatre of Dreams in 2017, but United opted for Romelu Lukaku instead. In the years since Rangnick's recommendation, the pressing-forward led Spain to European glory and sealed a move back to Italy, this time to multi-time Champions League winners, AC Milan. He quickly fell out of favour at the Serie A giants, though, and was shipped out on loan to Como at the beginning of the 2025/26 season.

Morata is now playing for Leganes, on loan from Como, in the second tier of Spanish football. File this one under 'bullet dodged', perhaps.

Christopher Nkunku could have become Manchester United’s first signing of the Ten Hag era after being one of RB Leipzig’s most notable stars. The Frenchman had a plethora of big-name clubs vying for his signature as he spearheaded Leipzig to a top-four finish in back-to-back seasons between 2021 and 2023, scoring a respectable total of 70 goals during his time at the club.

Injuries plagued the forward during his ill-fated spell with Chelsea, which left him determined to resurrect his career in Serie A. He scored eight goals in 35 games for Milan last season but is now back on loan with RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga.

Christopher Nkunku scored his third Premier League goal of the season as Chelsea beat Brighton at the Amex Stadium.

Imposing centre-forward Dusan Vlahovic, who was tipped to become a star on football's biggest stages, could have been a Manchester United player had the club been keen to listen more to Rangnick's transfer advice. Currently plying his trade in Turkey for Besiktas, the 26-year-old was previously one of Serie A's most recognisable forwards, despite struggling to show the same potency as he did during his time at Fiorentina.

Once on Arsenal's radar, there's still a chance that fans will get to see Vlahovic in the Premier League one day. But for now he's focused on scoring goals in the Turkish Super Lig.

All statistics courtesy of Transfermarkt - accurate as of 10/11/2026.

Mauricio Pochettino's first starting XI at Tottenham: Where are they now?

📅 2023-08-10  |  Read Source →

Where there's a project, there's usually a Mauricio Pochettino. Think Tottenham Hotspur and the success the Lilywhites very nearly had, Chelsea's billionaires, the American national team and, of course, Manchester United.

The Argentine has a track record of coming in as the deadwood removal man, transforming mediocrity into top-four competitors within a matter of a few transfer windows.

His time at Tottenham is a case study of how to fully maximise resources at a manager’s disposal. The Man United boss took the North London club all the way to Premier League title races and Champions League finals, albeit before falling at the final hurdle in heartbreaking fashion.

Upon taking over at Spurs in 2014, the former Southampton and Espanyol boss was inheriting a side that was a confusion of talented misfits and average footballing journeymen who arguably, weren’t fit for purpose.

Joining a club who were yo-yo-ing between Europa League finishes and occasionally qualifying for the Champions League, Pochettino was the catalyst that took Tottenham from a big club to a part of Europe’s elite. But where are his first Spurs starting XI now?

The passionate, forthright Frenchman was a mainstay in North London for what seemed like an eternity. The 6’2 goalkeeper signed from Lyon in 2012 and only left the club in 2023.

Having won a World Cup and a Nations League since, a trophy at domestic level sadly still eluded him. The closest that the Frenchman came to sealing glory for Spurs came in the Champions League final defeat against Liverpool.

At his best Lloris' acrobatic reflexes, bionic reaction time, and ability to read the game from his box forged a reputation for him as one of the best goalkeepers on the planet, especially under Pochettino.

Tottenham had an inexplicable habit of fielding right-backs named Kyle during the mid-2010s, with Naughton, Walker, and Walker-Peters all playing a part for the Whites at some point or another under Pochettino's rule.

It just so happened to be Kyle of the Naughton kind for Poch’s first game in charge, but the starting right-back would quickly fall out-of-favour, and arguably, didn’t make the best first impression under his new manager after being sent off in their 1-0 win over West Ham United.

Naughton would eventually head for North Wales in 2015, joining then-Premier League side, Swansea City. The player spent 10 years at the Liberty Stadium, but is currently without a club after admitting that he is 90% sure he's done with football in his late 30s.

Younes Kaboul was somewhat of a throwback at centre-half, big, bustling, and aerially dominant, the Frenchman was one of the last defenders from the school of Terry Butcher, with the blood-soaked bandage wrapped around his scarred head, all-black boots, and no-nonsense attitude, so understandably, was a natural choice as Pochettino’s first captain.

When he wasn’t injured, he was a solidifying presence at the back. However, just a short while after Pochettino’s introduction, the France international made the move up North for a short spell at Sunderland where he was part of a team that kept the Black Cats in the Premier League.

His North East stint didn't last for long, finding himself unable to resist the pull of the South, and what had been his home for the five years preceding. Heading to Watford to the tune of £4 million, the player appeared for the Hornets on just 26 occasions, before retiring thereafter.

Along with his old pal, Hugo, Eric Dier enjoyed a long stint at Tottenham. Pochettino's debut was also, in fact, Dier’s debut for the Lilywhites, and one where he certainly endeared himself to his new support, being the only player on the scoresheet in the 1-0 win.

The Englishman spent as many as 10 years in North London, before securing a surprise move to Bayern Munich. It was there that he linked up with former teammate Harry Kane to win the Bundesliga. Since then, Dier has swapped Munich for Monaco, who he joined in 2025.

Danny Rose’s career started with a very literal bang, with a scorching volley against old foes, Arsenal in a 2-1 win. It could be argued the left-back peaked too soon, but the fact he was a Poch-favourite and a continued selection for the England squad perhaps attested otherwise.

After that infamous meeting with manager, Jose Mourinho captured on the All or Nothing Amazon Prime sports docuseries, the boy from Doncaster’s career seemingly fizzled out following a string of second-rate moves to Newcastle and Watford, before retiring in 2022.

The Niort-born former French international was one of the duds signed with the world-record fee of £85 million the club secured for Gareth Bale. In what transpired to be an underwhelming acquisition, the defensive midfielder’s £9.5 million transfer flattered to deceive in a Spurs shirt.

The player appeared for Tottenham on just 36 occasions during his two-year stint in North London. Since then, Capoue has gone on to play for both Watford and Villareal, starring in the latter’s Europa League win over Manchester United in 2021, before retiring in 2024.

Like that of his midfield counterpart, Nabil Bentaleb’s Spurs career was short-lived, moving on in 2016 with a loan move to Schalke, followed by a permanent move to the then-Bundesliga club.

After a brief loan back in England at Newcastle, the midfielder found a more permanent home with Ligue 2 side, Angers before climbing back up to the top-flight by joining LOSC Lille, where he has been since 2023.

Now in his 30s, the midfielder has come full-circle and may well end his career in France.

Christian Eriksen presents one of the more intriguing tales in this Spurs XI. The attacking midfielder was a shining light during Pochettino’s tenure.

An expert passer, peerless playmaker, and visionary footballer, the Dane was one of the standout players in the Tottenham team that made it to the Champions League final and challenged for the league title.

Departing Hotspur Way shortly after his former manager, Eriksen joined up with Italian giants, Inter in 2020. After an unremarkable start to his Italian campaign, a chain of events followed that were by their very definition, remarkable.

Collapsing on the pitch in Denmark’s Euro 2020 opener due to a near-fatal heart attack, Eriksen was essentially dead for five minutes, with his teammates and home crowd watching on with their mouths agape. Resuscitated by medics, the former Tottenham man made a miraculous recovery and was fitted with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator.

Since then, the Dane has enjoyed spells at Brentford, Man United and Wolfsburg, but is currently without a club after collapsing again in 2026.

There was an air of world-beater about Aaron Lennon when he got going. A fullback’s worst nightmare the tricky, explosive winger had a killer delivery, and an immense low centre of gravity allowing him to almost glide between defenders.

The player left Tottenham in 2015, joining Everton and then Burnley. Lennon announced his retirement in 2022, regularly speaks about his experiences with mental health issues, and has taken it upon himself to raise awareness around a topic that has become increasingly less taboo.

“Everywhere you go, always take Lamela with you” was an inspired chant to the tune of Crowded House’s 1991 hit, Weather With You.

The left midfielder has bags of natural flair, and an over-abundance of ability. However, a mixture of inconsistency and a procession of injuries meant that White Hart Lane rarely got to see the Argentinian midfielder at the peak of his powers.

Lamela left on a free transfer in 2021, joining Sevilla where he won the Europa League, before joining AEK Athens and then retiring.

His football story didn't end there, however. The former Spurs man went onto become the assistant manager back at Sevilla in 2025 and then took on the same role at Monterrey in 2026, joining up with Matias Almeyda twice.

The 7 Best Pubic Hair Trimmers in 2026, Tested by Grooming Editors

📅 2023-07-24  |  Read Source →

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

These are the only tools I trust near my, er, tool.

LISTEN, NO ONE is going to say you must trim your pubic hair, but a little over half of all men do. Shaving, trimming, or hell, even getting a manzillian, comes down to a personal decision in both the how and why. Some guys like the way it feels, some like the way it looks, and some get a confidence boost knowing that they’re well-groomed down there. Whatever your reasons for below-the-belt manscaping, the most important thing to consider before you start is what tools you’re going to use to do it.

Trimmers are a great option for body grooming because they offer a variety of options. Most of them, at least the ones designed for the delicate groin area, have features to help protect the skin on your penis, scrotum, and surrounding areas from nicks and cuts.

They also usually have length attachments so you can choose exactly how long you want your hair (and even change it up as desired). Still, if you favor a close, hairless shave, you may want to turn to your old standbys: a razor and shaving cream. Whichever tool you ultimately choose will come down to a few factors based on your unique preferences. These are the seven best options across the board.

When it comes to pubic hair trimming, it’s all about balancing risk versus results. When you’re trimming or shaving delicate skin below the belt, you need to be careful, and this trimmer helps minimize risk. Specifically designed for your groin area, the blades are more closely spaced to help prevent snags, and the attachments help protect your skin from direct contact with the razor.

Testing Notes: This trimmer makes the case for using tools specifically designed for the area you’re grooming. I found in my testing that its blades are more closely placed than your traditional trimmer to help prevent skin from being caught between them. They actually make a difference when trimming your delicate nether regions.

All the features packed into this trimmer make the experience of trimming your groin as easy as possible and minimize cut risk, while the skin-protecting attachment does a great job of providing further distance between your skin and the blade. The one thing to note about this trimmer, however, is that if you prefer a clean shave, this will not deliver it by itself.

While it will trim very close, even with the attachment, it’s not going to give you a smooth, clean finish. You may want to use this trimmer to trim down the carpet first before moving in with a traditional razor. Also, if you’re hoping to trim other parts of your body, like your head or face (which I wouldn’t recommend for sanitary reasons), you may not find this trimmer powerful enough for the thicker hair that’s found in those locations.

Honestly, is there something the Philips OneBlade can’t do? Since its launch, this trimmer and shaver has become an iconic grooming essential, and for good reason. It’s incredibly easy to use, hardly ever nicks or cuts skin, and can shave and trim with equally good results. This version even comes with more length attachments that allow you to get your ideal manscaping results with ease.

Testing Notes: In all of my trimmer and shaver testing, no matter what kind, the Philips OneBlade stands out among the pack because it’s just so darn easy to use. Unlike your typical trimmers, the innovative head is shaped like a razor and can cut hair in both directions, making it foolproof.

There is also something about the razor, even when used without any attachments, that hardly ever cuts skin, even when you’re using it on your delicate areas below the belt. Since it’s designed for body grooming, the OneBlade features more attachments than the original, but you still won’t be able to leave hair super long.

The plus side of getting quite as close as other trimming options means it’s nearly impossible to cut yourself—even if you’re using it without a guard. Whenever someone is nervous about nicking their nuts, this is my top recommendation.

It’s best for people who like a close trim or a shave. The small size and light weight make it easy to take with you wherever you go, and I had no issue with the battery life, even though it’s not quite as long as some others on this list.

I also appreciate that it comes with a second blade, so you can easily switch them when you use this on your face (you don’t want to use the same blade on your face and body because of the possibility of cross-contamination).

Read more: Philips Norelco OneBlade Review

This trimmer is chock-full of cool features that are the sort of thing you didn’t know you needed until you have them, like a built-in LED light for seamless groinal navigation, a travel lock to avoid slicing through clothes or other products in your Dopp kit, and a nifty low-battery light to let you know it’s time to recharge before diving into a trim.

This trimmer is built for below-the-belt grooming but works great on other body parts too. It trims quickly and efficiently, no matter where you use it. The 5.0 is also fully waterproof and armed with a protective outer guard above the blades to minimize the risk of nicks or cuts.

Testing Notes: In my testing, I found a lot to love about the newest version of the Lawn Mower. Compared to previous models, it seems to cut a little bit easier and more efficiently, and with less snagging. The blade guard really does help in this department, though I did experience a few nicks when trying to trim too quickly (never a good idea when dealing with the groin, to be honest).

I don’t recommend using it without the guard, as the blades can be a little harsh on bare skin. However, a natural side effect of this is that you won’t ever get a completely bald shave with this device. Still, it’s surprisingly lightweight, and the added features like the built-in light make the experience of groin trimming as pleasant as it can be. It also corrected one of the more annoying issues with previous models by adding a travel lock on its power button that requires more effort to activate.

Unlike previous models, the 5.0 does not include a charging dock; however, it is fully equipped with USB-C charging capabilities, which I much prefer to the dock. I’d argue that every electric device should be required to use this much more universal charger. It saves on space by limiting the amount of wires you need laying around, and is far more convenient to replace if you ever lose the included cord.

Read More: Manscaped Chairman Plus Review

Meridian’s body trimmer helps prevent irritation, tugging, and nicks with its high-precision ceramic blades. Slicing your skin when manscaping, especially if you’re new to it, can produce serious panic, which is why Meridian went with ceramic blades. In comparison to steel or plastic, ceramic blades stay sharper longer, generate less heat, and glide smoothly across sensitive skin.

This makes Meridian’s trimmer ideal for beginners or anyone nervous about trimming sensitive areas. Plus, it’s waterproof and easy to use. There aren’t any complicated settings or tech involved, and just two guards to choose from. For beginners, this is perfect. It limits any learning curve beyond getting over the initial hump of anxiety for where you’re taking a blade.

Testing Notes: Meridian highlights two key benefits of its pubic trimmer: safety and speed—even claiming you can finish a full job in under 60 seconds. While I can confirm it’s powerful enough to mow through hair fast, no one should approach grooming with that expectation. Rushing, especially on sensitive areas, is a quick way to end up with nicks and cuts.

In terms of safety, I found this trimmer rarely—if ever—caused cuts or irritation. However, that safety seems to come at the cost of precision. I often had to go over the same spot multiple times to get a close shave. While the ceramic blades boost protection, they just don’t shave as closely as stainless steel.

Braun built this trimmer to power through all kinds of hair, no matter the length or location. With adjustable settings offering up to 40 lengths, it trims nose hairs just as easily as it delivers a crew cut. Its powerful motor and precision make it a top choice for anyone with thick body hair or an untamed look down below, where other trimmers often fall short.

Testing Notes: I love the wide-ranging length options the Braun All-In-One Series 9 offers that allow for true head-to-toe grooming. The adjustable length dial particularly makes transitioning from one part of your body to another seamless and quick for those in a hurry. Now, I wouldn’t recommend using the same trimmer for your face and body, but this device certainly has the agility and horsepower to handle all areas smoothly.

I also dig how sleek the charging dock is and, crucially, how little space it takes up on the bathroom counter. That being said, while Braun boasts about the Series 9’s 180-minute charging runtime, my testing found it’s in the 120-minute range. Still an impressive burst from one charge, but not quite 180 minutes.

Read More: Braun Series 9 Style Kit Review

Using a disposable razor for pubic shaving is great because it minimizes the risk of cross-contamination, and you ensure that your blades are always sharp and ready to cut. This disposable razor has five gentle blades that, while not specifically designed for the groin, are designed for the most sensitive skin, making it perfect for the area.

Testing Notes: Conventional wisdom says that using fewer blades is ideal for shaving the pubic area, as razors with multiple blades often increase the risk of irritation, razor bumps, and ingrown hairs. These issues tend to arise when the blades cut hair beneath the skin’s surface, creating friction and complicating regrowth.

In contrast, a single- or double-blade razor trims hair cleanly at the surface, reducing skin damage and delivering a smoother, gentler shave. But I found the BIC Flex 5 Sensitive razor to be the best of both worlds. Covering the ground of a five-blade razor with the softness of a one-blade razor.

Not only did it speed up the admittedly long process of pubic shaving, but it did so without destroying my most delicate skin. The only trade-off here is that this razor doesn’t get quite as close as other, less-gentle blades. Still, it gets much closer than the trimmers on this list, and nearly as close as the Gillette Intimate Razor. Besides, going entirely bald down here is rarely a goal of mine, so I saw this as a positive.

If you’re looking to go as close to bald as possible, this is your best option. Designed specifically for body grooming, this razor features a compact, ultra-grippy handle that minimizes the risk of dropping and helps you maintain control while in the shower (or contorting yourself to reach every part of your groin). The blades are about as spaced out from each other as I’ve seen on any razor, which helps prevent clogging—something that is even more common when dealing with thick body hair.

Surrounding the two blades are a lubricating strip, an anti-ingrown bar, and an anti-irritation bar that work to reduce friction and help prevent trapped hairs. Plus, the blade head sits on a flexible pivoting disc, which helps the razor follow the contours of your body for smoother, more consistent contact with the skin.

Testing Notes: I’m not usually one to go completely bald below the waist, but this razor makes a strong case for it. It left my skin smooth and irritation-free without any lingering bumps in the days following, which is something I’ve found to be common when dealing with body razors. The grip is incredible and the pivoting head makes getting into the nooks and crannies of your body easy.

Before diving into the most intimate of manscaping, it’s important to consider a few key components of the device you’ll be using, given the sensitivity of the region. Not only to avoid any dreaded nicks or cuts, but also to ensure that the process is completed as seamlessly as possible.

Whenever you’re dealing with a trimmer of any kind, the battery life is one of the most prominent considerations. No one wants their device to sputter out and die when they’ve only managed to trim half their beard, and the same is true for the nether regions. Sure, it may be less noticeable than having half a beard, but it can still be uncomfortable. Look for devices that can hold a charge for at least an hour; this should guarantee you two to three sessions per charge.

Any less and you’re going to have to really be diligent with charging after every use or run the risk of it dying out before the next job’s done. The easiest way to avoid this scenario is to look for a rechargeable device, but more on that in a sec.

If you’re a committed pubic trimmer and never travel without one, look for the lighter options to ensure you can comfortably keep them in a carry-on or bag without weighing yourself down. While the TSA and airlines do not generally have a weight limit specifically for grooming devices, they do limit the weight of your bags, so we recommend sticking to trimmers that are under 10 oz to avoid too much bulk. Plus, if you’re new to this type of thing, steering away from tools that are heavier than this until you get a better idea of the process will help you avoid any painful slip-ups.

Similarly, how often do you change up your overall manscaping look? If you find yourself often changing up lengths and styles, you’re going to want to grab a device with multiple attachments and length options. The Braun Series 9 is the best-case scenario here, as it comes packed with nine attachments that create a total of 40 (!) length options. On the other hand, if you typically go full bald or keep it one consistent length, focus on the device’s head shape and blade material or close shaving ability rather than the number of attachments.

For the closest shave (outside of a cartridge razor), look to stainless steel or metal blades, as these can handle the most motor power and are more adept at plowing through thicker hair. While most of the trimmers on this list (and pubic trimmers in general) do not list their official motor power, having stainless steel blades is often the best indicator of a powerful tool, as it shows the brand looks towards the highest quality materials and performance available.

Not to mention, stainless steel blades are typically easier to clean. That being said, the risk of nicks and cuts is higher, so if you’re new to pubic trimming, opt for ceramic or plastic blades. These are gentler on skin, though they won’t get you as close to bare skin.

Use a rechargeable pubic trimmer to avoid mid-trim shutdowns and eliminate the need for spare batteries. Keep it charged between 30 percent and 80 percent to maintain performance and prevent it from dying when you need it most.

Do you prefer to do your manscaping in or outside of the shower? There is no wrong answer, but whichever you prefer is worth keeping in mind when choosing a trimmer. Some are made to be used wet, like the Philips Norelco OneBlade, while others not so much. If you’re a dedicated shower groomer, focus on the fully waterproof options.

As Men’s Health’s grooming editor, I test electric razors and similar devices for a living. When it comes to pubic trimmers, we’ve been testing these devices for nearly three years since this story was first published in 2023. For this update, I tested or retested over 15 pubic trimmers and razors, while consulting with skin and haircare experts on which tools they recommend in 2026.

I also considered top-reviewed trimmers that had high customer ratings on trusted e-commerce websites. After putting each device to the test, I evaluated its effectiveness, safety, and value. Following 12 months of testing, these seven tools proved to be the best for the job.

1. First and foremost, make sure you have ample time and are not rushed. This is not something you want to speed through.

2. Position yourself in front of a mirror with good lighting to make sure you have good visibility for all the crevices.

3. Grab your trimmer and pick your desired length. If you plan to fully shave your pubic hair, set the length long enough to shave easily but not too long—about a couple of days’ worth of stubble. If you’re trimming, start with a longer setting than you want at first; you can always trim it shorter later.

4. Apply baby powder on your pubic area while it’s dry to help soak up extra moisture and plump up the hair.

5. With short, gentle strokes, use the trimmer to cut the hair. Pubic hair grows in a variety of directions, so you’ll want to go slow and possibly go over the same areas a few times. For your scrotum and shaft, go extra slow and stretch the skin to flatten it and make it easier to trim. If you’re trimming your buttcheeks, crack, or perineum, you may want to place a hand mirror on the floor to help see where you’re trimming. You can also place one leg on a tub or toilet to make the area easier to see.

6. If you’re happy with the trim job, then you’re done! Hop in the shower to wash off.

7. If you’re going to shave completely, once you’re out of the shower, apply a pre-shave oil and shaving cream to the areas you’re going to shave. The key here is not to be stingy with the cream.

8. When you’re taking a razor to your nether regions, you’ll want to be extra careful. Shave with the grain of the hair in short, slow strokes. Do not—I repeat—do not rush. You’ll want to use the same stretching technique on your scrotum and shaft as you did while trimming, and the mirror is ideal if you’re taking the razor around back.

9. Make sure to rinse the razor frequently to avoid clogs and reapply shaving cream as needed.

10. Once you’re done, hop back in the shower to rinse everything away.

11. Apply a moisturizer or body oil to the area to help keep it protected. You may also want to apply a moisturizer or anti-chafe product regularly (like at least once a day) to help reduce friction, which can cause irritation on shaved skin, especially below the belt.

Maybe you’re a regular manscaper, or perhaps you just took the plunge into trimming out your nether regions. Regardless, one truth holds true: As soon as you take off the hair, it blooms right back again.

Sure, it might seem that your pubic hair is on a steroid-fueled regrowth. But that’s actually something of an optic illusion, says Dr. Alexes Hazen, MD, a reconstructive and cosmetic plastic surgeon at NYU Langone Health.

People who trim or shave their pubic hair often believe it grows faster than the hair on their head, but that’s a misconception, she says. We merely notice hair growth more and its speed when it’s shorter.

With pubic hair—and other body hair—the entire process takes about 30 to 44 days, Dr. Hazen says. That means the same pubes that started to grow will shed in about a month to a month and a half.

Every Golden Boy Winner (Ranked)

📅 2023-07-06  |  Read Source →

The Golden Boy Award, created by the Italian publication Tuttosport, is awarded to the most talented under-21 player each year. Often used as a marker for players potentially destined for greatness, multiple icons of the game have collected the honour since its creation.

The prestigious accolade is awarded to a player in Europe by an assortment of journalists. Over the years, some huge names have lifted the trophy, including the likes of Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Erling Haaland. And Pau Cubarsi became the latest name to pick up the award in 2026.

What happens next, though, is anybody's guess. While some winners have blossomed, others have bombed, spectacularly failing to live up to expectations. And with 24 winners to pick from, every winner of the Golden Boy award has now been ranked.

There were two main things considered when ranking players:

Every Golden Boy Winner Ranked From Worst to Best

The winners of the Golden Boy award have experienced mixed career paths.

Sir Alex Ferguson possessed the inexplicable power of making average players look good. While Anderson was by no means average when he claimed the Golden Boy honour in 2008 after shooting to stardom with Porto and then United, his career soon fell into the depths of mediocrity.

During his eight years at Old Trafford, silverware did fall his way, but minutes in the league started to dry up as he became a bit-part player for Ferguson and then subsequent United managers.

Michael Owen went on the record in 2018, stating that while Anderson was "too relaxed" to become the best. Leaving the club in 2015 to return to Brazil, stints at Cortiba, Internacional and then finally Turkish side Adana Demirspor eventually led to him retiring in 2019.

When Anthony Martial announced himself to the world on his debut at Manchester United, scoring against the Red Devils' nemesis, Liverpool, many thought he was going to be the next big thing. He secured the Golden Boy award shortly after, and with a Ballon d'Or bonus inserted into the deal United made with Monaco, many thought the most prestigious individual prize in football could be next.

Although the French international started his time at Old Trafford brightly, torrid luck with injuries and examples of noncompliance resulted in a lacklustre career. Relegated to the role of an unused squad player by Erik ten Hag during his final campaign at the club, those promising days in 2015 feel oh so long away now.

It turns out it really has always been him, even when it came to the Golden Boy Award. Possibly the most charismatic and enigmatic of its long list of winners, Mario Balotelli took home the golden statuette in 2010 in the aftermath of Inter Milan’s historic European treble. However, controversy was never far away from the Italian throughout his career, be it parking fines galore or fans burning his shirt.

Ultimately, he failed to live up to the expectations that many had for him. Despite some notable moments of success, fans will always think about what Balotelli might have been if he had the right mentality.

Balotelli delivered fireworks both on and off the pitch for Manchester City, leading to his iconic celebration.

There was real fanfare surrounding the Portuguese international before his Golden Boy triumph, having already won the Euros with Portugal earlier in the year. Renato Sanches is a technically dexterous player, whose ability to manipulate the ball while dribbling with it is mesmeric. Saying that, his inconsistency has plagued his career, as have multiple injuries.

Without a club after leaving Paris Saint-Germain, a player once considered the best young star in the world now has no choice but to wonder what might have been.

Bought by Atletico Madrid for £113m from Benfica in 2019, Joao Felix has flattered to deceive ever since collecting the award.

As one of the most expensive teenagers of all time, the weight of expectation has clearly been felt, and his time at Atletico Madrid was thoroughly disenchanting. Despite winning the Spanish giants’ Player of the Season Award for 2021/22, the Portuguese international was then loaned out to Chelsea after a reported bust-up with head coach Diego Simeone.

His time in the Premier League didn't grab the right headlines, either, but the forward has since finally rediscovered his best form in Saudi Arabia for Al-Nassr in a move that no one expected him to be making by this stage of his career.

Lean, quick and lethal in front of goal, Alexandre Pato shot onto the scene in Serie A after signing for AC Milan for £24m, netting 51 times in 117 Serie A games for the Rossoneri.

Winning the award in 2009, the forward’s spell in Northern Italy was seemingly a one-off, and he was unable to settle down and achieve the same feat at any other club.

Alexandre Pato career goals (all competitions)

Following stints at Chelsea and Villarreal, he returned to his native Brazil and signed for Sao Paulo. There were two years at MLS side Orlando City sandwiched in-between, but Pato has few regrets. Speaking about his career in 2022, he shrugged: "The way I see it, I have a lot of Ballon d'Ors. If life is a game, I have won."

With a name like Rafael van der Vaart, the Dutchman was destined to be memorable. The first-ever winner of the award in question, the 109-cap Netherlands international rose through the ranks at Ajax and went on to play for clubs like Tottenham Hotspur, Real Madrid and Hamburg. He was some player on his day, capable of scoring rockets when he felt like it.

With 545 appearances, 174 goals, and 120 assists to his name by the end of his career, he decided to hang up his boots for good in 2018 following a brief spell at the Danish side, Esbjerg fB. Sure, he might not be the best Golden Boy winner of all time, but he was still a quality player.

You'd think scoring the winning goal in a World Cup final at the age of 22 would translate to a fruitful career. Sadly, for Mario Gotze, just one player tipped for greatness in 2012, his time as a professional footballer has been a tale of untapped potential and a string of injuries since he sealed the deal for his nation in Brazil.

The period between winning the Golden Boy accolade and holding the World Cup aloft was perhaps his most profitable as a player, winning consecutive Bundesliga titles with Borussia Dortmund and finishing runner-up in the Champions League final.

Now in his mid-30s, he is still plying his trade in the German top flight with Eintracht Frankfurt but has hardly had the career many thought he would have had when he found the back of the net against Argentina in 2014.

Only eight lucky nations have won football's ultimate prize.

There will be those of you who look specifically at Isco's time at Real Madrid and think he failed to live up to expectations. He won the Golden Boy award just a year after signing for Malaga, and in 2013, he was an integral part of Spain's U21 European Championship win.

However, while it is true he didn't quite reach the heights expected of him at Madrid, becoming more of a squad player in his last few years at Los Blancos and only hitting 53 goals and 57 assists during his nine-year career at the Bernabeu, he did play a part in all five of his Champions League wins with Madrid.

And now, after a tough time at Sevilla, where he claimed a director assaulted him, he rediscovered his best form at Real Betis and is a La Liga standout once again.

The Ajax side of 2018/19 had the football sphere reverberating with enthusiasm. Erik ten Hag’s young, fearless, and exciting side that played with that kind of naive freedom few teams do these days made a refreshing change. Matthijs de Ligt was a cornerstone of that team, and regardless of his tender years, featured in 55 games for the Amsterdam outfit.

A move to Juventus proved to be underwhelming, however, with the Dutchman never looking as assured at the back as he did for Ajax. There were also struggles during his two years at Bayern Munich, before a now injury-plagued spell at Man United.

GIVEMESPORT Key Statistic: Only five players have a higher combined transfer fee total than Matthijs de Ligt (£169m) - Alvaro Morata, Ousmane Dembele, Cristiano Ronaldo, Romelu Lukaku and Neymar.

Mastering the Art: How Real Estate Agents Should Write Facebook Ad Copy

📅 2023-06-07  |  Read Source →

In the digital age, social media platforms have become powerful tools for real estate agents to market their listings and attract potential clients. Among the various platforms available, Facebook remains a dominant force with its massive user base and advertising capabilities. To stand out in the competitive real estate market, agents must not only create compelling visual content but also craft persuasive ad copy that engages and captivates their target audience. In this article, we will delve into the key elements and strategies for writing effective Facebook ad copy, equipping real estate agents with the knowledge to maximize their advertising efforts and generate leads.

The first step to writing compelling Facebook ad copy is gaining a deep understanding of your target audience. By knowing their demographics, preferences, and pain points, you can tailor your copy to resonate with their needs and desires. Conduct thorough market research, utilize Facebook's audience insights, and analyze data from previous campaigns to gather valuable information about your target audience.

The headline is the first element of your Facebook ad copy that users will see. It needs to be attention-grabbing and compelling enough to entice people to read further. Use action-oriented words, emphasize unique selling propositions, and create a sense of urgency to pique the audience's curiosity and encourage them to click on your ad.

When writing Facebook ad copy, it's crucial to highlight the benefits of the property or service you're promoting, rather than merely listing its features. Benefits explain how the property or service can improve the lives of potential buyers or renters. By emphasizing the value and advantages, you can create an emotional connection with your audience and motivate them to take action.

Storytelling is a powerful tool for capturing the attention of your audience and making your Facebook ad copy more relatable. Craft a compelling narrative that showcases the unique aspects of the property or the positive experiences of previous clients. Engaging stories can evoke emotions, create a sense of authenticity, and build trust with potential clients.

In the fast-paced world of social media, attention spans are limited. To ensure your Facebook ad copy is effective, keep it concise and clear. Use short sentences and paragraphs, bullet points, and subheadings to enhance readability. Avoid jargon and technical terms that may confuse or alienate your audience.

Social proof, such as testimonials, reviews, or success stories, can significantly influence potential clients' decision-making process. Incorporate social proof into your Facebook ad copy to build credibility and trust. Highlight positive feedback from satisfied clients or showcase awards and recognition you've received in the real estate industry.

To encourage immediate action from your audience, create a sense of urgency in your Facebook ad copy. Limited-time offers exclusive deals, or a countdown timer can instill a fear of missing out (FOMO) and prompt potential clients to take the desired action promptly.

An effective call-to-action (CTA) is vital to prompt users to take the desired action, whether it's contacting you, visiting a landing page, or scheduling a property viewing. Use action verbs, provide clear instructions, and create a sense of urgency to motivate users to click on your CTA button.

Continuous testing and optimization are essential for improving the performance of your Facebook ad copy. Create multiple variations of your ad copy, test them against each other, and analyze the results. Fine-tune your copy based on metrics such as click-through rates (CTR), conversion rates, and engagement levels to identify what resonates best with your audience.

Writing compelling Facebook ad copy is a crucial skill for real estate agents looking to excel in their digital marketing efforts. By understanding their target audience, crafting attention-grabbing headlines, focusing on benefits, incorporating storytelling techniques, and utilizing social proof, agents can create persuasive and engaging copy that captivates potential clients. Remember to keep your copy concise and clear, create a sense of urgency, and use compelling calls to action. Through A/B testing and continuous optimization, agents can refine their ad copy to maximize its effectiveness. By mastering the art of writing Facebook ad copy, real estate agents can unlock the full potential of social media advertising and boost their success in the competitive real estate market.

A common mistake people make when moving is to pack all of their belongings and move them, only to realize upon unpacking that many of the items should have been donated, sold, or thrown out. Before you pack, ruthlessly declutter your home. Packing things only to get rid of them at the new house is a waste of your time and money.

Greg Dallaire - Green Bay Real Estate Expert says, "Be sure to set up any utilities in the new place to be turned on and ready when you arrive. Even if it means paying for utilities at two places for a brief overlap, it is often worth the convenience. In addition to basics like water and power, call ahead to make sure you will have internet, TV, and any other services you need."

This is also a great time to move additional services to the new address, like security, pest control, or house cleaning.

Even if you are moving all in one day from one Calgary home to another, don't count on being able to unpack everything you need on night one.
